runs.sourceText: THE CORE IDEA

transcript.text: THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Supply describes the quantities sellers are willing and able to offer at different prices, holding other supply conditions constant. Quantity supplied is the amount sellers offer at one particular price. The law of supply states that a higher own price generally increases quantity supplied and a lower own price decreases it, all else equal. An own-price change causes movement between points on the same supply curve; it does not shift the curve.
